prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: approval mockup of the proposed Arcane Emporium magic shop interior in Stone & Shadow, a first-person C++ grid-based dungeon crawler. One wide 16:9 landscape environmental concept, not a screenshot.
Input images: Image 1 actual Sanctuary inn capture is a SCALE AND GAME STYLE reference only: modest human-sized furniture, simple prepared geometry, clear broad circulation, warm painted surfaces. Image 2 approved smithy interior concept is an ART STYLE reference only: cohesive handmade stone, lime plaster, oak beams and textured painterly materials. Create a new room, not a smithy or tavern, and do not copy HUD.
Primary request: a compact, inviting medieval fantasy MAGIC SHOP selling potions, spell scrolls, magical books and small arcane supplies, replacing the town's provisioner. Blend an apothecary's practical workroom with a wizard's tidy retail shop, grounded in the same modest Sanctuary buildings. Pale aged plaster between dark oak beams, lower grey stone courses, low timber-beamed ceiling, worn flat grey stone floor flags. Restrained indigo fabric accents, brass/copper and small jewel-colored glass bottles, parchment cream. Soft daylight and warm lamplight, with only a little teal/purple magical glow. Detailed hand-painted mildly pixelated game textures on simple low-poly forms, feasible classic dungeon-crawler art.
Layout: view straight into a rectangular room from just inside its entrance, at ordinary standing human eye level. Keep a broad straight TWO-CELL-WIDE central aisle completely empty from entrance to the customer standing position at a low wooden service counter near the back centre-right. The waist-high counter is shallow, WELL BELOW eye line, with an indigo inset panel bearing a small restrained gold star motif. Behind its middle leave a clear EMPTY human standing space facing the entrance, a full future NPC silhouette space above and behind the counter. Beyond that is a wall of shallow potion shelves and drawers, not furniture intruding into the merchant standing space. The counter stops short of the right wall so there is a full one-cell-wide staff bypass leading behind it.
At the left perimeter: a compact wooden scroll cabinet with square cubbies containing rolled parchment and a short run of book shelves; several upright scroll cases and sealed scroll rolls, all human-sized and readable. At right perimeter: one compact waist-height alchemy workbench against the wall, a SMALL copper alembic with flask and glass receiver, a mortar/pestle, ingredient jars and a neat bundle of dried herbs above. A small shuttered leaded window on that wall brings daylight. A modest potion display shelf against left rear wall has a few red, blue, green and amber bottles grouped tidily. Limit room dressing to clear practical clusters; keep free floor and staff routes intact.
Scale and movement: all cabinets/workstations form straight RECTANGULAR whole-cell footprints aligned with walls; the floor is flat, no steps/platforms. No freestanding central island, furniture on diagonals, narrow curved route, obstacles, rugs or floor clutter. A human fits behind the counter and can reach the workbench around its right end. Bottles are hand-sized, books and scrolls ordinary-sized, workbench/counter human waist-high; never giant flask sculptures or oversize books. Architecture similar ceiling height to the supplied references, not a cathedral.
Composition: show the whole usable room, empty central approach and empty merchant spot clearly. Mild downward framing, horizon about 40 percent from top, no aerial/isometric view or ultra-wide lens. Scrolls at left, merchant counter rear, alchemy bench right. Cozy, quietly magical, maintained and welcoming rather than sinister.
Constraints: NO people, NPCs, pets, floating books or hovering objects. No HUD, lettering, readable text, annotations, watermark or logo. No rations, sacks of flour, bread, produce, inn tables, weapon racks or forge. No cinematic bloom, fog, neon light, elaborate high-poly machinery or photorealistic PBR. Generate a polished concept approval image, not a top-down floor plan.
